sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Kendall County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Deeds for Kendall County property are recorded at the County Recorder's office at 502 S Main St in Yorkville, the county seat. The same elected officer serves as County Clerk and Recorder, so you will see both titles on county signs and web pages.

The office phone for recording questions is 630-553-4112, and the county lists general hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The research area is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office stops taking plats at 3:00 p.m. and other documents at 4:00 p.m., so a deed that arrives at 4:15 waits for the next business day. The recorder's page states plainly that staff give no legal advice and run no document searches for the public, so questions about what a deed should say belong with an attorney or a title company.

sections.h2: What does Kendall County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A deed costs $76.00 to record in Kendall County under the fee schedule the Recorder posts. Most other common documents land at the same price, and a few special categories cost less or more.

Kendall County Recorder fee schedule, effective July 1, 2023 (source: Kendall County Recorder fee schedule)
DocumentFee
Deed$76.00
Mortgage, assignment, subordination, modification or release$76.00
Easement (not filed by a government body)$76.00
Transfer on death instrument$76.00
Mechanic lien$76.00
Tax lien$57.00
Government or utility filing exempt from the rental housing surcharge$57.00
Re-recording of a document$57.00
Non-standard document$88.00
Plat$110.00 base
Military dischargeNo fee

Five parcel numbers are included in the price. Each extra parcel number adds $1.00, which matters for a sale that covers a house plus an adjoining lot. A certified copy costs $27.00 for the first four pages and $1.00 for each page after that, and plain photocopies run $0.50 a page.

sections.h2: When does a Kendall County recording cost extra?
sections.html:
A document that fails the format rules is charged as a non-standard document, which adds $12.00 to the $76.00 deed fee and brings the total to the $88.00 shown above. The schedule lists the problems that trigger it:

  • A page size other than 8.5 by 11 inches
  • Ink that is not black or blue
  • Type smaller than 10 point
  • No blank space in the upper right corner of the first page for the recording stamp
  • Tape, stickers, labels or greyed areas on the page

Plats follow a separate rule: subdivision and condominium plats need the original plus two copies and a letter from the surveyor giving permission to record, while other plats need the original plus one copy. Every additional plat page is $1.00. Only originals or certified copies are accepted, never a plain photocopy of a signed deed. Mail-in packages need a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return, and a second envelope if you want copies sent back.

sections.h2: What paperwork travels with a Kendall County deed?
sections.html:
A sale deed normally goes in with a PTAX-203 transfer declaration, or with a signed exemption statement when the transfer qualifies for one. The recorder's page links a list of PTAX-203 exemptions along with sample quit claim and warranty deed forms, a Plat Act affidavit and a redaction request form.

The page does not spell out a full checklist of what a deed must contain, so confirm with the closing attorney or title company before sending a package. Staff can look at a finished document and reject it if something is missing, but they cannot draft it. Foreclosure notices are a separate track: the County Clerk's page says all notices of foreclosure go to the Office of the Kendall County Clerk at the same Main Street address.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Kendall County sale?
sections.html:
The state tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, collected by the county recorder under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, with counties issuing electronic stamps or another proof of payment afterward.

The Kendall County Recorder began using MyDec for online PTAX-203 declarations on December 2, 2019. MyDec sends the declaration through the Illinois Department of Revenue, and under the same statute every recorded sale must be reported to the Department electronically. Some deeds are exempt from the tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, including deeds where the real consideration is under $100, tax deeds, deeds of partition, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder in a foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. Even then, a deed for a government or charitable transfer, a like-kind exchange, or a Home Ownership Made Easy Act purchase still needs the declaration filed.

Ask the Recorder, or the village or city hall where the house sits, whether any local stamp or exemption certificate applies before closing day.

sections.h2: Can you record a Kendall County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, the Recorder's page links to the electronic recording services of CSC and Hopdox, and the office also points users to the county's online land records search. Electronic recording runs through a vendor account held by a title company, lender or attorney, so a homeowner usually benefits without setting anything up personally.

The office also offers Property Fraud Alert, a free service that notifies a property owner of recording activity connected to their name. Owners who sell or inherit property in the county can sign up through the link on the recorder's page. It is a quick way to see that a deed or lien you did not expect has been filed against your name.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Kendall County itself?
sections.html:
Kendall County is a small county of 320 land square miles that sits in the Chicago metropolitan area. It was formed in 1841 from LaSalle and Kane Counties, and Yorkville is the seat. Oswego is the largest municipality. Plano, Montgomery, Minooka, Newark, Plattville and Lisbon are among the other communities, and parts of Aurora, Joliet and Plainfield reach into the county.

The county has grown fast. It went from 54,544 residents in 2000 to 131,869 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 145,470. The northeast and the Fox River corridor hold most of the people, while the south stays largely agricultural.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures give an owner-occupied rate of 84.0%, a median home value of $322,400 and median household income of $111,601. The bureau counted 733 building permits in 2025 and a mean commute of 31.6 minutes, a sign that many residents work outside the county. The county is split between two community college districts: Waubonsee Community College serves the north half and Joliet Junior College the south.

sections.h2: Where do Kendall County property tax and assessment questions go?
sections.html:
Recording is separate from tax billing. The county site has distinct pages for the Treasurer, the assessment offices, the township assessors and the Board of Review, and the Treasurer's pages cover payment, due dates and the annual tax sale.

  • Unpaid tax on the parcel: ask the Kendall County Treasurer for the current balance before closing.
  • An assessment you think is wrong: start with the township assessor, then the Board of Review.
  • A missing homestead exemption: ask the county assessment office.
  • A changed name or mailing address on the bill: ask the County Clerk or Treasurer.

Closing agents usually order the tax search and the payoff, so the seller's job is mostly to hand over the parcel number from the tax bill.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Kendall County, Illinois?
faqs.a: A deed costs $76.00 to record under the schedule effective July 1, 2023. The fee rises to $88.00 when the document is non-standard, and each parcel number beyond five adds $1.00.

faqs.q: Does the Kendall County Recorder accept photocopies of a deed?
faqs.a: No, the office accepts only originals or certified copies. A self-addressed stamped envelope is required to get the recorded document back by mail.

faqs.q: What time does the Kendall County Recorder stop accepting documents?
faqs.a: Documents are accepted until 4:00 p.m. on weekdays and plats until 3:00 p.m. The research area is open from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I file the Illinois transfer declaration online in Kendall County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder has used MyDec for online PTAX-203 declarations since December 2, 2019, and the form is processed through the Illinois Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Kendall County recording?
faqs.a: Call the Recorder's office at 630-553-4112. For anything about what a deed must say, the office points callers to an attorney because staff cannot give legal advice.
